title: Prediction Error
subtitle: The gap between expectation and outcome
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical neuroscience diagram illustrating prediction error across threat, memory, regulation and treatment systems.
tags: established learning signal; broader theory mixed
searchTerms: established learning signal; broader theory mixed
learningObjectives: Explain prediction error in clinically accurate language.
Distinguish established findings from theoretical or mixed claims in prediction error.
Identify one limitation or safety implication relevant to prediction error.

sections.explainSimply: Prediction error occurs when reality differs from what the brain expected.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Corrective experiences are most informative when a feared prediction is clearly specified and then disconfirmed.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Predictive-processing accounts are influential but broad; clinical claims should be tied to observable expectations and outcomes.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Think of prediction error as one part of a dynamic safety-and-learning system rather than a single switch.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need prediction error to connect symptoms with learning, context, risk and treatment choice without reducing the person to a brain scan.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Surprise alone is not therapeutic; safety, meaning and integration matter.
sections.clinicalPearl: Clinical pearl: use prediction error to sharpen formulation, not to replace phenomenology or outcome measurement.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician uses prediction error to formulate triggers, state shifts, avoidance and functional impact, then monitors whether intervention improves daily life rather than relying on presumed neural change.
sections.limitationsCautions: Surprise alone is not therapeutic; safety, meaning and integration matter. Evidence classification: established learning signal; broader theory mixed.
